content.summary_of_the_paper:
In the paper, a scalable uplift modeling is proposed to improve the predication accuracy of uplift values in the domain of business marketing.
In the experiments, the authors show that GNN-based uplift network reaches good performance.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
I feel this paper is either written within a very stringent time limit or the author(s) lack scientific writing experiences. To begin with:

1. The citation formality is overall incorrect, which has been clearly discussed in the ICLR template.
2. Regarding the mathematical format of latex environment, unconventional math expressions have been widely used such as Eq. 13 Dim[g], 
uncommon fonts 'ITE' and 'CATE' used in Eq. 2 and 3, 'where' in Eq. 24. 

Besides, the implementation details of the proposed approach is largely unknown and not presented in the paper. 

Last, I am uncertain how this specific approach used for business purpose can reach large impact in the scientific community.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
Overall, the quality of this paper is not satisfactory and below the acceptance threshold.
The reviewer finds  its hard to evaluate the reproducibility and have concerns on the impact to the scientific community.
content.summary_of_the_review: Based on above evaluations, I am afraid I cannot recommend this paper for acceptance without essential revision of the current manuscript.
content.correctness: 2: Several of the paper’s claims are incorrect or not well-supported.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.

display_title: Official Review of Paper2811 by Reviewer X1aK

content.confidence: 3: You are fairly confident in your assessment. It is possible that you did not understand some parts of the submission or that you are unfamiliar with some pieces of related work. Math/other details were not carefully checked.
content.summary_of_the_paper: The paper addresses the problem of uplift modelling. The authors propose a framework that involves estimating conditional average treatment effects, which are then used as feature attributes. Moreover, the proposed method uses graph neural networks over the learnt causal graph of the data to predict uplift values.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengths:
- The paper addresses an important problem

Weaknesses:
- It is not clear why building a causal graph and using a graph convolutional network is needed to estimate the outcomes; in particular, why is it the case that standard methods that just use the features as input fail and a graph approach is needed? 
- The authors propose using "conditional average treatment effect (CATE) as the attribute representing the causal information of the feature”; however, it is not clear here with respect to that is this causal average treatment effect and why it is useful to use it as a feature attribute. 
- Learning the causal structure of the data requires strong assumptions (needed to identify the causal graph) which the authors do not mention in the paper; similarly, strong assumptions are also needed to identify the conditional average treatment effects which the paper does not mention. 
- The related works section makes it difficult to understand what the novel contributions of the proposed method is over prior works in uplift value estimation. 
- In the experiment section, the synthetic dataset used for evaluation has a very simple form. thus, it is unclear how using Graph Convolutional Networks improves estimation in that case. Moreover, the baselines used for comparing performance are very simple and no other methods in uplift value estimation are benchmarked against.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
Clarity:
- The paper mentions that they increase the "amount of data information by defining causal knowledge and implementing structured representation”; it is not clear how this increases the data information? 
- The paper has several typos both in the text (e.g. ‘Shere’ instead of where) and in equations (e.g. equation (3))
- The paper is lacking references; For instance, it mentions that "In the past, researchers in uplift modelling were largely concerned with how to employ unbiased data and models in the estimation framework” without providing any reference to such methods, which makes it hard to judge the novelty of the work. 
- The paper is also missing information about the model hyperparameters used which hinders reproducibility.
content.summary_of_the_review: Overall I believe that the paper in its current format is not ready for publication. The paper would significantly benefit from better explanation of the proposed approach and its assumptions, better description of relevant literature and stronger evaluation setting.
content.correctness: 2: Several of the paper’s claims are incorrect or not well-supported.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 1: The contributions are neither significant nor novel.

content.confidence: 3: You are fairly confident in your assessment. It is possible that you did not understand some parts of the submission or that you are unfamiliar with some pieces of related work. Math/other details were not carefully checked.
content.summary_of_the_paper: The paper studies the problem of uplift modeling. The paper develops a causal representation method based on conditional average treatment effect estimation and Bayesian network learning. These causal knowledge are combined with graph convolutional network for uplift modeling. Some experiments are further provided to validate the resulting method.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
The idea of using GNN for uplift modelling with causal knowledge seems intuitive. However, the paper has many weaknesses:
- Many of the ideas or modelling choice seem very adhoc and not justified. E.g., in Section 3.1 "We estimate each feature’s ... This work has been proven to obtain more information", no citation/reference was provided. For the few paragraphs in Section 3.1 that describe Figure 1, it seems that these paragraphs just describe the procedure without proving a detailed explanation of the motivation of the modeling choice, which therefore make them sound adhoc.
- This is also the case for Sections 3.2 and 3.3. It is not convincing why using the learned Bayesian network structure in the GCN is a good choice.
    - The baseline should also include using GAT (https://arxiv.org/abs/1710.10903) without a predefined structure or GSL (https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.03036) that learns a structure, in order to show that using GCN with a Bayesian network structure is useful.
- Many of the details and terminologies are not explained in a clear way and may require the readers to guess, some of which may not be common in the causality literature. Examples:
    - What is a "causal value" in Figure 3?
    - Why is the adjacency matrix in Figure 3 a vector but not a matrix?
    - What are "causal weights"?
    - What are "multi-head causal graph" or "multi-head mechanism"?
    - What does it mean for every feature to have a causal graph? (In causal graph learning, there is only one causal graph over all variables.)
    - What are "soft label" and "knowledge label"?
    -  What adjacency matrix $A$ does the GCN use? I guess it's the causal graph learned in Section 3.2, but this is not explicitly stated. Also, the causal graph learned is a binary matrix, so is $A$ a binary matrix? Since causal graph is directed, can GCN handle directed graph (see https://arxiv.org/abs/2004.13970, https://arxiv.org/abs/2101.07965)?
- The abstract claims that the proposed framework is more scalable. However, I did not find any experiment related to scalability.
- Related works in the intersection of GNN and causality are not discussed, such as https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.04173, https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.10098, https://arxiv.org/abs/1911.07420, https://arxiv.org/abs/2104.06643
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The clarify of the paper could probably be improved, since many explanations are missing, as described in the section above. Given that many modelling choices are not justified or explained clearly, the quality and novel are limited.
content.summary_of_the_review: The key points of my comments are provided in the sections above.
content.correctness: 2: Several of the paper’s claims are incorrect or not well-supported.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.
